content: {"rule":"K-C","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The text rules on Link 6 (Isaiah 7:14), where the defender's chain (8:3, 8:8, 9:6-7) collides with the challenger's chain on the sign's bounds.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"the sign itself does not state the mechanism","rule_words":"the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires","room":"'weighs chain against chain by footing': the judge names both sides' rows ([CR2]'s 8:8 and 9:6-7, [DR3]'s bounds), which could read as weighing chains; but it never compares their footing and rests the outcome on what the single verse states, so I read it as the retired test.","why":"The judge settles the collision with the stating-verse test, that Isaiah 7:14 does not itself state the mechanism, and does not weigh the two chains by footing."}
